candidates.candidateFocus: Commitment status of a considered course of action
semanticRelations: The target concerns a course of action that is still being weighed.
No relation presents the course of action as already adopted.
The present stance is the act of consideration itself.
candidates.decisionBasis: The visible structure establishes a tentative stance as the current status, so interpretation can proceed without treating the lack of adoption as interpretive uncertainty.

candidates.candidateFocus: Commitment status of a proposed course of action
semanticRelations: The target concerns a course of action first introduced as a proposal.
A later approving response may address either the proposal or only the preceding discussion.
No relation specifies whether the proposal itself became the adopted stance.
candidates.decisionBasis: The visible structure leaves the decision-relevant adoption relation undetermined, so the current commitment status cannot be selected.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status of a provisional preference
semanticRelations: A preference is presented with an explicit provisional qualifier.
The qualifier applies to the preference rather than to a separate alternative.
No later relation removes or upgrades the provisional status.
candidates.decisionBasis: The provisional status is itself the established interpretation; finality is not required for CLEAR.

candidates.candidateFocus: Adoption status after acknowledgment
semanticRelations: A suggested stance is followed by an acknowledgment.
The acknowledgment can attach to receipt of the suggestion or to acceptance of it.
No relation distinguishes receipt from adoption.
candidates.decisionBasis: The status that matters for downstream classification is whether the stance was adopted; the visible evidence leaves that relation open.

candidates.candidateFocus: Standing of an explicitly rejected option
semanticRelations: The target option is placed in a set of possibilities.
A later relation excludes that option from the user's current stance.
No relation reintroduces the option as active.
candidates.decisionBasis: The negative current status is established; CLEAR does not require a positive adopted preference.

candidates.candidateFocus: Current status of a deliberately postponed decision
semanticRelations: The target decision is explicitly deferred.
The deferral is presented as the current stance toward the decision.
No relation claims a selection was made elsewhere.
candidates.decisionBasis: A known postponement is a determinate interpretation for the ambiguity stage.

candidates.candidateFocus: Whether a preference statement is exploratory or settled
semanticRelations: One relation presents attraction to a stance.
Another relation requests comparison with alternatives.
The visible structure does not state whether attraction is only exploratory or the current chosen stance.
candidates.decisionBasis: The decision-relevant status between exploration and chosen preference is not established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Commitment status after explicit confirmation
semanticRelations: A possible action is introduced before a later confirmation.
The confirmation directly targets the same action.
No relation limits the confirmation to discussion-only acknowledgment.
candidates.decisionBasis: The adoption relation is present in the visible structure.

candidates.candidateFocus: Whether a conditional plan has become active
semanticRelations: The target action is tied to a prerequisite condition.
A later relation says the topic should be kept in mind.
No relation says whether the prerequisite condition now holds.
candidates.decisionBasis: The active commitment status depends on a condition whose status is not visible.

candidates.candidateFocus: Current-state relation after an explicit replacement
semanticRelations: An earlier state is stated for the target.
A later state is introduced as replacing the earlier one.
The replacement relation applies to the same target and same dimension.
candidates.decisionBasis: Precedence is established by the replacement relation, so there is one current interpretation.

candidates.candidateFocus: Current-state relation between two incompatible statements
semanticRelations: An earlier state is stated for the target.
A later incompatible state concerns the same target and same dimension.
No relation marks either statement as replacing, correcting, or limiting the other.
candidates.decisionBasis: The visible structure gives incompatible states without an applicable precedence relation.

candidates.candidateFocus: Coexistence of two dimension-specific updates
semanticRelations: One relation updates a first dimension of the target.
A second relation updates a different dimension of the same target.
The dimensions do not compete for the same slot.
candidates.decisionBasis: The two updates coexist because they apply to separate dimensions.

candidates.candidateFocus: Precedence between a correction and a reiterated older state
semanticRelations: A correction relation changes the target state.
A later relation repeats the older state without saying it is a retraction or reminder.
The visible structure does not specify whether the repetition supersedes or merely restates stale wording.
candidates.decisionBasis: The applicable current relation between correction and later repetition is not established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status of an explicitly retracted prior claim
semanticRelations: A prior claim is tied to the target.
A later relation retracts that prior claim.
No replacement claim is needed to know the prior claim no longer stands.
candidates.decisionBasis: The retraction establishes the current status of the old claim.

candidates.candidateFocus: Relation between a broad update and an earlier specific exception
semanticRelations: An earlier relation creates a specific exception for the target.
A later broad update addresses the surrounding category.
No relation says whether the broad update removes, preserves, or bypasses the exception.
candidates.decisionBasis: The current status of the exception is decision-relevant and not established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Which of two same-dimension states currently applies
semanticRelations: Two relations assign different values to the same target dimension.
Both relations are presented as current-facing.
The visible structure supplies no correction, recency, or scope relation that selects one.
candidates.decisionBasis: The same dimension has competing current-facing assignments with no precedence relation.

candidates.candidateFocus: Current relation after narrowing a broad statement
semanticRelations: A broad state is stated for a category.
A later relation narrows that state to a specific subcase.
The narrowing relation is presented as the applicable refinement.
candidates.decisionBasis: The broad claim and later refinement have an established precedence relation.

candidates.candidateFocus: Whether two asserted differences are conflict or independent updates
semanticRelations: Two relations describe changes involving the same target.
The first relation concerns a property that may overlap with the second relation's property.
The visible structure does not specify whether the properties are the same dimension or separate dimensions.
candidates.decisionBasis: Without the dimension relation, coexistence versus conflict cannot be determined.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status of a durable default with a bounded exception
semanticRelations: A default pattern is stated for the target.
A separate relation creates an exception with a bounded interval.
The exception is tied to the interval rather than replacing the default.
candidates.decisionBasis: The relation between default and bounded exception is explicit, so persistence status is established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status of a changed pattern after a one-time departure
semanticRelations: A default pattern is stated for the target.
A later relation describes a departure from that pattern.
No relation says whether the departure is a bounded exception or the new ongoing pattern.
candidates.decisionBasis: The visible structure does not establish exception versus replacement.

candidates.candidateFocus: Meaning of a temporary state
semanticRelations: The target state is explicitly tied to a limited period.
The limited period is part of the asserted status.
No relation presents the state as continuing beyond that period.
candidates.decisionBasis: Temporary status is established and does not by itself require escalation.

candidates.candidateFocus: Whether a recurring behavior persists after a disruption
semanticRelations: A recurring behavior is stated for the target.
A later relation says the behavior stopped during a circumstance.
No relation says whether the behavior resumed, stayed stopped, or became conditional after the circumstance.
candidates.decisionBasis: The persistence status after the disruption is decision-relevant and not visible.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status of a one-off exception
semanticRelations: A usual pattern is established for the target.
A later relation marks a single occurrence as departing from the pattern.
The departure is not presented as changing the usual pattern.
candidates.decisionBasis: The one-off exception relation is established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status of a future bounded interval
semanticRelations: The target state is assigned only to a future interval.
The interval boundary is part of the stated relation.
No relation claims the state already applies outside that interval.
candidates.decisionBasis: The future-limited applicability is the established status.

candidates.candidateFocus: Whether a pause is temporary or indefinite
semanticRelations: A previously recurring pattern is followed by a pause relation.
The pause relation does not include a boundary, trigger, or replacement pattern.
No later relation supplies a status after the pause begins.
candidates.decisionBasis: The persistence status cannot be determined from the visible relations.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status of a recurring behavior with stated cadence
semanticRelations: The target behavior is described as recurring.
A cadence relation attaches to that behavior.
No exception or stop relation competes with the cadence.
candidates.decisionBasis: The recurring status and cadence relation are established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Applicability of an exception after a broad restatement
semanticRelations: A default state is followed by an exception relation.
A later broad restatement repeats the default state.
The visible structure does not say whether the restatement includes or excludes the exception case.
candidates.decisionBasis: The exception's continuing applicability is not established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Referent of a target expression after a single active antecedent
semanticRelations: The target expression refers back to a prior mentioned item.
Only one prior item has the required semantic role.
No competing antecedent matches that role.
candidates.decisionBasis: The visible antecedent structure selects one referent.

candidates.candidateFocus: Referent of a target expression with multiple active antecedents
semanticRelations: The target expression refers back to a prior mentioned item.
Two prior items both have the required semantic role.
No relation chooses between the two items for the target expression.
candidates.decisionBasis: The visible structure leaves multiple materially plausible referents.

candidates.candidateFocus: Target of an elliptical confirmation
semanticRelations: A question introduces one candidate target.
The following elliptical confirmation occurs in direct response to that question.
No intervening relation introduces another candidate target.
candidates.decisionBasis: Adjacency and question-answer relation identify the target.

candidates.candidateFocus: Target of an elliptical confirmation after multiple prompts
semanticRelations: Two candidate targets are introduced before an elliptical confirmation.
The confirmation is compatible with either target.
No relation indicates which prompt the confirmation answers.
candidates.decisionBasis: The target of the confirmation is not recoverable from visible relations.

candidates.candidateFocus: Referent of a comparative expression
semanticRelations: The target expression is comparative.
The comparison set contains a single previously mentioned alternative.
The compared property is shared by the target and that alternative.
candidates.decisionBasis: The comparison relation identifies the referent.

candidates.candidateFocus: Referent of a role-based expression
semanticRelations: The target expression selects an entity by role.
More than one active entity has that role.
No relation marks one role-holder as the active target.
candidates.decisionBasis: Multiple role-compatible referents remain.

candidates.candidateFocus: Referent after a topic shift
semanticRelations: A target expression follows a topic shift.
An older antecedent and a newer antecedent both match the expression's semantic type.
No relation states whether the expression continues the old topic or attaches to the new one.
candidates.decisionBasis: The topic-shift relation does not select one antecedent.

candidates.candidateFocus: Referent of a repeated shorthand label
semanticRelations: A shorthand label is introduced for one target.
The same shorthand is later used without any competing label assignment.
No other active target is assigned that shorthand.
candidates.decisionBasis: The label assignment relation supplies the referent.

candidates.candidateFocus: Referent of a category shorthand
semanticRelations: The target expression names a category rather than a unique item.
Several active items belong to that category.
No relation narrows the category to a single item or intended subset.
candidates.decisionBasis: The category reference has materially multiple possible targets.

candidates.candidateFocus: Applicability of a rule with an explicitly attached exception
semanticRelations: A general rule applies to a category.
An exception relation is attached to a named subcategory.
The target belongs to the exception subcategory.
candidates.decisionBasis: The applicability relation is established by category membership and exception attachment.

candidates.candidateFocus: Applicability of a rule with a possible exception
semanticRelations: A general rule applies to a category.
An exception relation is attached to a subcategory.
The target may or may not belong to that exception subcategory, and no membership relation is provided.
candidates.decisionBasis: The rule's applicability depends on a membership relation absent from the visible structure.

candidates.candidateFocus: Scope of a constraint attached to a single target
semanticRelations: A constraint is stated immediately after one target is introduced.
The constraint repeats a property unique to that target.
No broader category is introduced for the constraint to attach to.
candidates.decisionBasis: The scope attachment points to the single target.

candidates.candidateFocus: Scope of a trailing qualifier
semanticRelations: A qualifier follows two coordinated targets.
The qualifier is semantically compatible with either the second target alone or both targets together.
No relation marks the qualifier's attachment boundary.
candidates.decisionBasis: The visible structure leaves the scope attachment materially indeterminate.

candidates.candidateFocus: Applicability of a specific override
semanticRelations: A broad rule is stated for a category.
A later specific rule targets the same item.
The specific rule is presented as taking precedence for that item.
candidates.decisionBasis: Specific override precedence is visible.

candidates.candidateFocus: Applicability of a general rule to a borderline member
semanticRelations: A general rule applies to members of a category.
The target shares some but not all defining relations of that category.
No relation states whether partial membership is sufficient for the rule.
candidates.decisionBasis: Applicability turns on category membership criteria that are not established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Scope of an instruction limited to a named subset
semanticRelations: An instruction is stated for a subset.
The target is identified as belonging to that subset.
No relation extends the instruction to the surrounding category.
candidates.decisionBasis: The subset membership and limited instruction scope are established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Applicability when an exception is explicitly excluded
semanticRelations: A rule applies to a category.
An exception exists for a subcategory.
The target is stated not to belong to the exception subcategory.
candidates.decisionBasis: The exclusion relation makes the rule applicable to the target.

candidates.candidateFocus: Which target a shared modifier limits
semanticRelations: A shared modifier appears after a list of targets.
The modifier can semantically restrict the entire list or only the final target.
No relation identifies the modifier's intended span.
candidates.decisionBasis: The modifier's scope is not established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Actuality status of example-only content
semanticRelations: The target content is introduced as an example scenario.
The example relation covers the state being judged.
No relation presents the state as the user's actual state.
candidates.decisionBasis: The non-actual example status is established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Actuality status of content adjacent to an example
semanticRelations: An example scenario is introduced before the target state appears.
The target state can be read as continuing the example or as a separate current assertion.
No relation closes the example frame or attaches the target state to it.
candidates.decisionBasis: The actual-user-state versus example-frame relation is not established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Actuality status of quoted content
semanticRelations: The target content is marked as someone else's quoted statement.
The quotation relation covers the state being judged.
No relation adopts the quoted state as the user's own state.
candidates.decisionBasis: The quotation frame establishes non-user actuality.

candidates.candidateFocus: Whether a reported state is adopted by the user
semanticRelations: The target state is attributed to another speaker.
A later relation expresses alignment with some part of that report.
No relation specifies whether the alignment adopts the target state itself.
candidates.decisionBasis: The user's actuality relation to the reported state is not established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status of a roleplay assertion
semanticRelations: A roleplay frame is active for the target content.
The target state belongs to the role assumed inside that frame.
No relation exits the roleplay frame before the target state.
candidates.decisionBasis: The roleplay frame establishes the actuality status.

candidates.candidateFocus: Actuality of a state after a hypothetical setup
semanticRelations: A hypothetical setup is introduced.
The target state follows after the setup.
No relation marks whether the target remains inside the hypothetical setup or returns to current assertion.
candidates.decisionBasis: The frame boundary around the target state is not visible.

candidates.candidateFocus: Actuality status of a historical report
semanticRelations: The target state is tied to a past interval.
The past interval relation is part of the asserted content.
No relation presents the state as current.
candidates.decisionBasis: Historical status is established; it is not current actuality ambiguity.

candidates.candidateFocus: Whether an observed system state reflects user state
semanticRelations: The target state is inferred from an observed system behavior.
The same behavior can result from user preference or from an external constraint.
No relation states which cause applies.
candidates.decisionBasis: The actuality of the user state depends on a cause relation not visible.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status of a target after mixed quotation and assertion
semanticRelations: A quoted state and a user-authored assertion appear in the same evidence bundle.
The target expression could point to either the quoted state or the user-authored assertion.
No relation links the target expression to one actuality frame.
candidates.decisionBasis: The target's actuality frame is not established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status established by two partial relations
semanticRelations: One relation identifies the target state.
A second relation supplies the missing qualifier needed for the same state.
The two relations attach to the same target and do not compete.
candidates.decisionBasis: The partial relations jointly establish one interpretation.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status requiring a missing qualifier relation
semanticRelations: One relation identifies the target state.
A second relation mentions a qualifier but does not attach it to the target state.
The target state has materially different interpretations depending on that attachment.
candidates.decisionBasis: A necessary relation is present only as an unattached qualifier, leaving the interpretation undecided.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status from confirming relations across fragments
semanticRelations: An initial relation states a candidate status for the target.
A later relation confirms the same target and status.
No relation introduces an alternative status for the target.
candidates.decisionBasis: Separate fragments reinforce the same status without conflict.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status when partial relations point to competing readings
semanticRelations: One relation supports a first status for the target.
Another relation supplies a qualifier compatible with a different status.
No relation states whether the qualifier modifies the first status or creates a separate status.
candidates.decisionBasis: The combination relation between partial evidence is not established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status from a target relation and an explicit boundary
semanticRelations: A target state is stated in one relation.
A boundary relation limits the same state.
The boundary relation explicitly attaches to the target state.
candidates.decisionBasis: The combined state plus boundary is visible.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status needing relation between two partial cues
semanticRelations: One cue supplies a target state.
Another cue supplies a condition that could govern that state.
No relation indicates whether the condition applies to the target state or to a neighboring state.
candidates.decisionBasis: The condition attachment is materially necessary and absent.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status from complementary identity and stance relations
semanticRelations: One relation identifies which target is being discussed.
A separate relation gives the stance toward that same target.
No other target competes for the stance relation.
candidates.decisionBasis: The identity and stance relations jointly establish the interpretation.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status from separated default and exception relations
semanticRelations: A default relation applies to the target category.
A later exception relation names the target as excluded.
The exception relation and default relation share the same governing dimension.
candidates.decisionBasis: Separated relations combine into one applicability status.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status when one necessary relation conflicts across fragments
semanticRelations: Two relations identify the same target.
One relation attaches a qualifier to the target while another attaches an incompatible qualifier.
No relation supplies precedence, timing, or coexistence between the qualifiers.
candidates.decisionBasis: The visible structure contains competing qualifier relations with no governing relation.

candidates.candidateFocus: Meaning of a coherent approximate range
semanticRelations: The target state is expressed as a bounded range.
The range is presented as the intended form of the state.
No relation introduces a competing exact value or different basis.
candidates.decisionBasis: Approximation is part of one established interpretation.

candidates.candidateFocus: Basis of a range with multiple possible meanings
semanticRelations: The target state is expressed as a bounded range.
The range can refer to either frequency or amount for the same target.
No relation identifies which dimension the range measures.
candidates.decisionBasis: The approximate form is acceptable, but its measurement basis is not established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status of an approximate cadence
semanticRelations: A recurring target is assigned an approximate cadence.
The approximation modifies the cadence rather than the target identity.
No relation supplies a conflicting cadence.
candidates.decisionBasis: The approximate cadence is coherent and visibly attached.

candidates.candidateFocus: Relation between two approximate alternatives
semanticRelations: Two approximate alternatives are stated for the same target.
The alternatives could be a range, a choice set, or a revision sequence.
No relation specifies how the alternatives relate.
candidates.decisionBasis: The decision-relevant relation between approximate alternatives is not established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Meaning of a deliberate loose threshold
semanticRelations: The target state includes a threshold described loosely.
The loose threshold is the stated decision boundary.
No relation introduces a second threshold basis.
candidates.decisionBasis: A loose but coherent threshold is not interpretive ambiguity.

candidates.candidateFocus: Unit of an approximate target value
semanticRelations: The target state includes an approximate value.
The value can plausibly use two different units in the visible structure.
No relation selects the unit.
candidates.decisionBasis: The unit relation is materially necessary and absent.

candidates.candidateFocus: Status of an open-ended approximate preference
semanticRelations: The target preference is expressed with an approximate lower boundary.
The boundary is attached to the preference scale.
No relation presents an incompatible scale or endpoint.
candidates.decisionBasis: The approximate lower boundary provides one coherent interpretation.

candidates.candidateFocus: Whether an approximate value is target state or example
semanticRelations: An approximate value appears near the target state.
The value can function as an example or as the actual target value.
No relation marks the value's role.
candidates.decisionBasis: The approximate value's semantic role is not established.

candidates.candidateFocus: Relation between an approximate point and a later range
semanticRelations: An approximate point is stated for the target.
A later range is stated for the same target.
No relation specifies whether the range refines, replaces, or merely illustrates the point.
candidates.decisionBasis: The relation between the point and range is decision-relevant and not visible.
